title: The effects of climate change could adversely affect JPMorganChase’s business and operations, both directly and as a result of impacts on its clients and customers.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Transition risks, including evolving regulatory requirements, carbon taxes and the adoption of new technologies to support lower-carbon operations, may increase compliance and operational costs, contribute to commodity price volatility
reason: Text is condensed and reworded; commodity price volatility overlaps the energy-cost exposure already covered, and dropped examples do not show the exposure shrinking.

title: The Company experiences cybersecurity incidents and inadvertent losses and unauthorized access to or releases of confidential information, including personal information.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the development, deployment and use of artificial intelligence by the Company, its employees and its suppliers exposes the Company to additional vulnerabilities and attacks
reason: This year adds AI as a new source of risk, both as an attack enabler and as an internal and supplier vulnerability. Last year's text did not address AI at all.

title: Our indemnification obligation to fund settlement losses of our clients, and in some cases other third parties, exposes us to significant risk of loss and may adversely impact our liquidity.
label: new_exposure
evidence: requirements that would obligate Visa to absorb certain settlement related losses for certain transactions involving sellers in Brazil when settlement failures occur
reason: New Central Bank of Brazil rules could require Visa to absorb settlement losses on Brazilian seller transactions, a loss source last year's text did not cover.

title: JPMorganChase faces significant legal risks from civil and governmental proceedings, including litigation, investigations and enforcement actions.
label: boilerplate
evidence: the extent of JPMorganChase’s exposure to legal matters is unpredictable and could, in some cases, exceed the amount of reserves
reason: The text is condensed and reworded; the core litigation, regulatory and penalty exposures remain, and dropped items are examples rather than a stated shrinkage of exposure.

title: JPMorganChase’s compliance risk and operating costs could be higher in jurisdictions with less predictable legal, regulatory and judicial frameworks.
label: boilerplate
evidence: there can be no assurance that JPMorganChase will always be successful in doing so
reason: The Russia litigation and asset seizure example was dropped, but the company does not say the exposure shrank. Otherwise the wording is condensed and reordered with no substantive change.

title: The issuance of our common stock upon conversion of our Mandatory convertible preferred stock, and the exchange of the Spirit Exchangeable Notes, as well as any other issuances of our common stock, could dilute the interests of our existing shareholders.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We may also issue shares of our common stock upon the exchange of the $230 million of 3.250% Exchangeable Notes
reason: The assumed $230 million Spirit Exchangeable Notes are a new, specific potential source of share issuance and dilution that last year's text did not name.

title: Other digital safety abuses
label: new_exposure
evidence: certain AI technologies, including conversational or emotionally engaging AI systems, may present distinct risks for children and adolescents
reason: Conversational and emotionally engaging AI systems are a new product category with child-safety risks that last year's text did not mention. Age-assurance obligations for app stores and operating systems are also new.

title: Delaware law, provisions in our governing documents and our capital structure could make a merger, takeover attempt or change in control difficult.
label: new_exposure
evidence: certain litigation against us or our directors, officers or other employees can only be brought in the state of Delaware or the U.S. federal courts
reason: A litigation forum restriction appears this year and was absent last year, limiting where shareholders can sue the company and its directors and officers.

title: We are subject to complex laws, rules, regulations, and political and other actions, including restrictions on the export of our products, which may adversely impact our business.
label: new_exposure
evidence: any H200 shipped under the new licensing program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States
reason: A 25% U.S. tariff on licensed H200 shipments is a new cost source for China sales that last year's risk factor did not mention.

title: Demand for our products and services may be impacted by the status of government and economic incentives supporting the development and adoption of such products.
label: new_exposure
evidence: If we or our suppliers are unable to provide sufficient documentation to verify the origin of critical minerals, our products may lose eligibility for tax credits and incentives
reason: Critical-mineral traceability rules under the OBBBA create a new loss source, lost tax-credit eligibility from documentation gaps, that last year's text did not cover.

title: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a holding company and depends on its subsidiaries for funding to make payments on its outstanding securities.
label: boilerplate
evidence: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. is subject to regulatory restrictions and requirements relating to the dividends that it can pay to the Parent Company
reason: Rewording and dropping the named SLR example; the dividend limits, payment restrictions, and bankruptcy-timing risk are substantively unchanged from last year.

title: Damage to JPMorganChase’s reputation could negatively affect its business, results and prospects.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Maintaining the trust, affinity and goodwill of clients, customers, employees and investors is critical
reason: The list of reputational sources was condensed and several items dropped, but the company does not say those exposures shrank or ended, and the remaining drivers were already covered.

title: Declines in U.S., global and regional economic conditions adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Past declines in economic conditions reduced or resulted in slower growth than expected in
reason: Rewording and condensing; dropped historical examples and the cost-structure plan reference without saying the exposure shrank, and the core risk drivers remain the same.

title: We face risks related to the protection and utilization of our intellectual property that may result in our business and operating results being harmed.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Our increasing engagement with open source software will also cause us to license our intellectual property rights broadly in certain situations.
reason: Two material drivers were dropped: changes in law weakening patent protection and open source licensing of IP. The company does not say the exposure shrank.

title: We must minimize disruption caused by production changes, achieve and maintain operational stability and implement productivity improvements to meet customer demand and maintain our profitability.
label: escalated
evidence: There is risk that planned production rate increases may be delayed or not occur at all if our production health key performance indicators and rate readiness process guided by our Safety Management System do not support increasing production rates or we are unable to obtain FAA concurrence.
reason: The same production-rate delay risk now attaches to specific, larger planned increases (737 to 47 per month, 787 increases) and to FAA concurrence, making it more concrete.

title: The Company’s future performance depends in part on support from third-party software developers.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the Company may earn a lower commission on such sales, or may not earn a commission at all
reason: Last year's text never addressed App Store commissions or alternative distribution and payment methods, so this creates a new revenue-loss exposure. The new fraud and AI-abuse risk is also new.

title: Competition and technology platforms' business practices:
label: escalated
evidence: California and New York passed the Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act and the Responsible AI Safety and Education Act, respectively, each of which imposes safety and reporting obligations on developers of frontier models
reason: State AI laws that last year were only possible ('some states may move to regulate') are now enacted, imposing concrete obligations, so the already-covered AI regulatory risk has materialised.

title: JPMorganChase’s business and operations rely on appropriate staffing and on the competence, trustworthiness, health and safety of employees.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including due to health emergencies or other extraordinary events beyond JPMorganChase’s control
reason: The list is condensed and some examples dropped, but the core workforce, staffing and conduct exposures are unchanged and the company does not say any exposure shrank.

title: Our success depends on our ability to develop, deliver, and maintain competitive cloud-based and AI products and services that achieve broad customer adoption and sustainable revenue growth.
label: escalated
evidence: which could result in reputational harm, regulatory scrutiny, service disruptions, or adverse impacts on our business
reason: The misuse risk now names regulatory scrutiny and service disruptions as concrete consequences, where last year it cited only reputational damage and general business impacts.

title: Failure to anticipate, adapt to or keep pace with new technologies in the payments industry could harm our business and impact future growth.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Our and our partners’ use of AI depends in part on third-party large language models that we do not control, whose models may generate inaccurate, biased, hallucinated or unexpected outputs
reason: The filing adds a new source of loss: reliance on third-party LLMs producing inaccurate or biased outputs, with reputational, regulatory and liability consequences that last year's text did not cover.

title: We may not realize the anticipated benefits of mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures/strategic alliances or divestitures.
label: new_exposure
evidence: we are required to provide services to buyers of divested Spirit businesses
reason: Service obligations to named buyers, including Airbus, with claims risk on nonperformance, are a new counterparty-specific source of loss not covered in last year's text.

title: Our Commercial Airplanes business depends on our ability to maintain a healthy production system, ensure every airplane in our production system conforms to exacting specifications, achieve planned production rate targets, successfully develop and certify new aircraft or new derivative aircraft, and meet or exceed stringent performance and reliability standards.
label: escalated
evidence: recognized additional reach-forward losses of $4.9 billion and $3.5 billion in 2025 and 2024
reason: The 777X program now shows concrete, already-realized losses of $4.9B and $3.5B, and delays are described as significant rather than general, so the risk has materialised.

title: JPMorganChase faces substantial legal and operational risks related to the processing and safeguarding of personal information.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The growing sophistication of technology poses a heightened risk of identity fraud
reason: The named AI driver was dropped, but the identity-fraud exposure, its consequences and the countermeasure language remain substantively unchanged, so the change is rewording rather than a shift in risk.

title: A successful cyber attack could cause significant harm to JPMorganChase and its clients and customers.
label: escalated
evidence: JPMorganChase could be required to make significant investments in technology in order to transition effectively to more robust security protections, including quantum-resistant encryption.
reason: The quantum exposure was already covered, but the text now adds a costly required transition and third-party laggards that could increase vulnerability to data compromise.

title: Our fixed-price contracts subject us to losses when we have cost overruns.
label: new_exposure
evidence: could trigger additional material earnings charges, termination provisions, order cancellations or other significant financial exposures
reason: New text cites termination provisions and order cancellations as loss sources not named last year, though it also drops the production, supplier and labor drivers.

title: JPMorganChase’s businesses could be adversely affected if it fails to identify and address operational risks associated with the introduction of or changes to products, services, delivery platforms or technologies.
label: escalated
evidence: has resulted and could in the future result in
reason: The added phrase "has resulted" says operational failures from these changes have already occurred, so the same exposure is now shown materialising. The new fraud-loss consequence reinforces this.

title: Resolving an investigation by a governmental authority could subject JPMorganChase to significant penalties and other repercussions.
label: new_exposure
evidence: criticism or litigation from clients or customers who claim that they have been harmed by actions taken by JPMorganChase in order to comply with applicable law
reason: Client litigation over harm caused by compliance actions is a new source of loss not covered last year, which named only regulatory penalties and litigation over the underlying conduct.

title: Government-imposed obligations and/or restrictions on international payments systems may prevent us from competing against providers in certain markets.
label: de_escalated
evidence: these restrictions on dual-branded cards have decreased our payments volume and impacted the net revenue we generate in China
reason: The revised text drops the statement that dual-brand restrictions already reduced volume and revenue, and it reports progress on the China BCCI application.

title: Some of our and our suppliers’ workforces are represented by labor unions. Work stoppages by our employees have adversely affected and could continue to adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows. Future work stoppages by our or our suppliers’ employees could also adversely impact our business.
label: escalated
evidence: went out on strike for 101 days, disrupting our St. Louis operations
reason: A second work stoppage, IAM District 837's 101-day strike, now materializes the previously described union risk with concrete program disruption, and the workforce share rose to 40%.

title: JPMorganChase's business and operations could be negatively affected by governmental policies that discourage or penalize doing business with certain industries or that require specific business practices.
label: boilerplate
evidence: harm to its reputation arising from public criticism, including from politicians, activists and other stakeholders
reason: Changes are rewording and dropped list items or examples (reputational-harm bullet, past-prohibition sentence) with no company statement that the exposure shrank or ended.

title: JPMorganChase’s ability to distribute capital to shareholders, and to support its business activities could be limited if it does not satisfy applicable regulatory capital requirements.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Although more likely in times of stress, JPMorganChase may use its regulatory capital buffers allowing capital ratios to decline below regulatory requirements, subjecting it to restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to its executive officers.
reason: New risk scenario: voluntarily or stress-driven use of regulatory buffers below requirements, triggering distribution and bonus restrictions, which last year's text did not mention.

title: Competition in the financial services industry could lead to negative effects on JPMorganChase’s results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: advocacy by non-banking competitors for exemptions from regulatory requirements could significantly disadvantage traditional financial institutions
reason: Regulatory-exemption advocacy by non-bank competitors is a new source of competitive loss not covered last year, alongside newly named generative AI and tokenized securities risks.

title: We are subject to complex and evolving global regulations that could harm our business and financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: require us to maintain additional capital or financial resources
reason: Last year's text never mentioned capital or financial resource requirements as a regulatory consequence, a new source of cost and loss for investors to weigh.

title: We may be subject to tax examinations or disputes, or changes in tax laws.
label: new_exposure
evidence: As we expand our business operations, we may be subject to new or additional tax reporting and compliance requirements, which could increase tax uncertainty and operational costs.
reason: New cost and uncertainty source from business expansion; permanent establishment and indirect tax disputes are also newly named, though the general tax-dispute risk was already covered.

title: JPMorganChase could incur significant losses arising from concentrations of credit and market risk.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the significant expansion of private credit could worsen losses among non-bank lenders and their borrowers
reason: This year adds private credit and non-bank lender losses as a new source of credit and market-making loss that last year's concentration risk text did not cover.

title: Future operating results depend upon the Company’s ability to obtain components, compute capacity and storage resources in sufficient quantities and on commercially reasonable terms.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The Company’s business, including its artificial intelligence and machine learning offerings, also depends on access to sufficient compute capacity and storage resources.
reason: Last year's text covered only physical components; this year adds third-party compute and storage capacity and data center infrastructure as a new source of supply and cost risk.

title: Our ability to adjust to evolving corporate responsibility and sustainability matters and related regulations could adversely affect our business and financial results or negatively impact our reputation.
label: boilerplate
evidence: may be or may become applicable to our business
reason: The changes are rewording and reordering of the same CRS regulatory, stakeholder and litigation risks; the hedged applicability and added general sentence don't alter substance.

title: A significant inadequacy in disclosure or financial reporting controls could negatively affect JPMorganChase’s business, operations and reputation.
label: boilerplate
evidence: JPMorganChase is subject to complex global financial reporting obligations that require continuous enhancements to disclosures
reason: The risk is the same: control lapses could cause inaccurate reporting and the same harms. The wording was condensed and the reputation and investor-confidence bullets were dropped, with no change in exposure.

title: Climate-related physical and transition risks could disrupt our businesses and adversely affect client activity levels and the creditworthiness of our clients and counterparties, and we are at increased risk of being subject to conflicting legal and regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations regarding climate-related matters.
label: de_escalated
evidence: we expect that climate change-related risks will increase over time
reason: This year's filing drops last year's outlook that climate risks will increase and omits the EU requirement to put a climate transition plan into effect, softening the forward-looking exposure.

title: We may experience outages, disruptions, or capacity constraints if we fail to maintain and operate adequate infrastructure or secure the resources necessary to support it.
label: new_exposure
evidence: we rely on third-party providers, including colocation facilities, leased datacenters, and cloud infrastructure providers, to support portions of our operations
reason: This year's text adds reliance on third-party colocation, leased and cloud providers, exposing the company to their outages, physical damage and cybersecurity incidents, which last year's text did not address.

title: Failure to meet the evolving needs of our industry and markets may adversely impact our financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We have entered into an intellectual property license arrangement with Groq, Inc., or Groq, that required significant, nonrefundable payments.
reason: A new counterparty and licensing arrangement with nonrefundable payments creates a loss source absent from last year's text, which only covered DGX Cloud generally.

title: U.S. HEALTHCARE REGULATION
label: new_exposure
evidence: the FDA's recently adopted policy of disclosing Complete Response Letters for unapproved drug candidates and the attendant risk of disclosure of trade secrets or confidential commercial information
reason: The FDA policy to disclose Complete Response Letters creates a trade secret and confidential information loss source that last year's text did not cover in any form.

title: Failure to effectively manage potential conflicts of interest or to satisfy fiduciary obligations could result in litigation and enforcement actions and cause reputational harm.
label: boilerplate
evidence: handle or use confidential information of customers or clients appropriately and in compliance with applicable law.
reason: Mostly rewording and condensing; the dropped client-data bullet and privacy-law reference are list and wording changes, with the confidential-information risk still covered and no stated shrinkage of exposure.

title: Other demand-related factors.
label: boilerplate
evidence: increased demand for artificial intelligence (AI), including the construction and expansion of AI data centers
reason: The added items (AI data center demand and strategic reserve builds) are upside demand drivers, not new sources of loss; other edits are minor wording.

title: We rely extensively on information and financial systems to process transactions, summarize results and manage our business. Disruptions in our systems could harm our ability to conduct our operations.
label: boilerplate
evidence: catastrophic events noted above in this Item 1A
reason: The list of catastrophic events and other examples was condensed by cross-reference, but the company does not say the exposure shrank, so no substantive change.

title: Any failure by us to comply with a variety of U.S. and international privacy and consumer protection laws may harm us.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Many other U.S. states have enacted their own distinct privacy laws and regulations, which often impose different, overlapping, and sometimes conflicting requirements
reason: Adds detail on multi-state privacy complexity, but state and cross-jurisdiction inconsistency were already covered; the Asia-Pacific wording is also a geographic broadening of existing exposure, not a new source of loss.

title: Due to the international nature of the Company's business, geopolitical or economic changes or events, including global tensions and war, could adversely affect our business, results of operations or financial condition.
label: new_exposure
evidence: including data localization laws and restrictions on data transfers
reason: Data localization and data-transfer restrictions are a distinct regulatory loss source not previously covered; dropped Russia and jurisdiction examples are boilerplate.

title: We derive a significant portion of our revenues from non-U.S. sales and are subject to the risks of doing business in other countries, including those related to tariffs, trade restrictions and government actions.
label: escalated
evidence: in the second quarter of 2025, certain customers in China paused accepting our deliveries in response to ongoing tariff negotiations between the U.S. and China
reason: Tariff exposure was already covered last year, but this year the risk has materialised: Chinese customers paused deliveries, and tariffs may now cause order terminations.

title: RESPONSIBLE BUSINESS PRACTICES
label: de_escalated
evidence: have differing views on matters perceived to be related to responsible business practices
reason: Stakeholder pressure is softened from 'increasingly sensitive' to 'differing views', and 'growing demand' and the proxy advisory reference were dropped.

title: We are exposed to fluctuations in the fair values of our investments and, in some instances, our financial statements incorporate inherently subjective valuation methodologies.
label: escalated
evidence: the value of our investments could significantly decline
reason: The closing risk statement now says investment value could significantly decline, a larger-magnitude wording than last year's plain decline; the other edits are rewording or dropped scope.

title: If we or third parties we rely on sustain cyberattacks or other privacy or data security incidents resulting in disruption to our operations or the misappropriation or disclosure of protected personal information or proprietary or confidential information, we could suffer a loss of revenue and increased costs, negative operational effects, exposure to significant liability, reputational harm and other serious negative consequences.
label: boilerplate
evidence: misplaced or lost data, human error, insider threat, malicious social engineering
reason: Changes are rewording and list additions, such as insider threat, within the already-covered risk of cyber compromise and vulnerabilities, with no change in substance or exposure size.

title: Our future growth and success are dependent upon demand for our electric vehicles and adoption of autonomous driving solutions.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Upon launching our Robotaxi service in June 2025, we also entered into the autonomous ride-hailing service market
reason: Robotaxi and Cybercab autonomous ride-hailing is a new business line with its own adoption risk that last year's risk factor did not cover.

title: We enter into cost-type contracts, which also carry risks.
label: boilerplate
evidence: each generated approximately 40% of their 2025 revenues from cost-type contracting arrangements
reason: Only the year and cost-type revenue percentages changed, and they moved in opposite directions (BDS down, BGS up), so the exposure size did not clearly shift.

title: The Company’s business and reputation are impacted by information technology system failures and network disruptions.
label: boilerplate
evidence: the implementation of upgrades or replacements to the Company’s global enterprise resource planning system may result in disruptions, cost overruns or data integrity failures
reason: System upgrades were already a covered source of failure last year; the ERP example is a new instance of that risk, not yet materialised, so it is not a new exposure.

title: If we do not address evolving consumer product and shopping preferences, our business could suffer.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The increasing use of data analytics, automation and artificial intelligence across digital platforms is further reshaping how consumers discover, evaluate and engage with brands.
reason: The added AI and affordability language extends drivers of the already-covered digital-shopping and consumer-preference exposure, without a new loss source or a stated change in its size.

title: Changes in our credit ratings or macroeconomic conditions may affect our liquidity, increasing borrowing costs and limiting our financing options.
label: escalated
evidence: in 2025, our rating was downgraded by S&P Global Ratings and Moody's Ratings
reason: Moody's has now also downgraded the company, so the credit-rating risk has materialised beyond last year's single S&P downgrade. The shift from 'will' to 'may' increase borrowing costs is a softening, but escalation ranks higher.

title: Access limitations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: directly or indirectly through the influence on these processes by well-funded local or international groups opposing the development of these resources
reason: Access restrictions can now arise from well-funded opposition groups influencing permitting, a cause last year's text did not mention in any form.

title: We may not be able to continue to successfully maintain or grow engaging third-party content on our platform or usage of and engagement with applications that integrate with our products.
label: new_exposure
evidence: we may not be successful in obtaining or attracting engaging third-party content
reason: The risk now covers creators supplying third-party content to the platform, a source of engagement dependence the prior text did not address.

title: Our financial results may be adversely affected if substantial investments in businesses and operations fail to produce expected returns.
label: boilerplate
evidence: or strategic initiative to provide expected returns or profitability, or to do so within anticipated timeframes
reason: The added wording widens the scope to strategic initiatives and timing, but the risk is the same failure-to-return exposure and the company does not describe it as larger or more likely.

title: Unfavorable media coverage negatively affects our business.
label: escalated
evidence: We have also been, and expect to continue to be, subject to media coverage in connection with litigation matters. For example, several bellwether trials in our youth-related litigation matters are scheduled for 2026 and beyond.
reason: Litigation was already a covered source of publicity, but the text now adds concrete youth-related bellwether trials and expects continued coverage, signalling a more active risk.

title: JPMorganChase’s results could be materially affected by market fluctuations and significant changes in the valuation of financial instruments.
label: boilerplate
evidence: may not always be effective, and it could incur significant losses
reason: Changes are mostly modal wording (may to could) and condensing, including dropping the stress-testing description; the exposure itself is unchanged.

title: Net-zero scenarios.
label: escalated
evidence: Society’s progress continues to lag in these areas.
reason: New text says policy-dependent progress toward net zero is already lagging and that net zero will remain out of reach for ExxonMobil, showing the transition risk is materialising.

title: Competition laws and new market regulation:
label: boilerplate
evidence: governments may impose restrictions on the development, deployment, availability, or cross-border access to advanced AI models
reason: The AI regulation-restricts-opportunity risk was already covered last year; the new restriction types are hypothetical examples of that source, not evidence it has materialised.

title: Sellers’ and processors’ continued push to lower acceptance costs and challenge industry practices could harm our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: sellers and seller-affiliated groups have exerted significant influence in the global payments system
reason: Changes are rewording, spelled-out EMV, and reordered sentences; the new 'significant influence' wording is a tone shift, not a change in the exposure itself.

title: Changes in technology, in consumer consumption patterns and in how entertainment products and services are created affect demand for, the revenue we can generate from and the cost of producing or distributing our entertainment offerings and our results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: In addition, the implementation of our DTC strategy may further contribute to such declines.
reason: The company now flags its DTC strategy as a further driver of linear declines, where last year it only noted forgone traditional revenue. This suggests a larger exposure.

title: Contentmoderation:
label: escalated
evidence: new regulations apply to online child safety, including access and content restrictions as well as other limitations for minors
reason: Child-safety rules moved from proposed focus to laws now applying, with concrete access and content restrictions added, though the cost reference was dropped.

title: Failure to successfully execute our omnichannel strategy and the cost of our investments in eCommerce and technology may materially adversely affect our market position, net sales and financial performance.
label: escalated
evidence: the increasing role of AI-enabled platforms in product search, discovery, advertising and purchasing
reason: The store-traffic risk from digital shifts is not new, but this year names AI-enabled platforms as an increasing, already-present driver of that shift, so the exposure is described as more likely.

title: We may be unable to effectively manage our liquidity, which could adversely affect our business, financial position and results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: approximately $15.5 billion of principal payments on outstanding debt are scheduled to become due over the next three years
reason: Scheduled debt maturities over three years rose from $13.6 billion to $15.5 billion, a clear increase in exposure, though the removed cash-burn and Spirit debt disclosures soften the picture.

title: The performance of strategic alliances and other business relationships to support the expansion of our business could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
label: boilerplate
evidence: These arrangements (such as ONE, our fintech venture) may not generate
reason: The only change is dropping the named example ONE from last year's text; the company does not say the exposure shrank or ended, so substance is unchanged.

title: The growth of electronic trading and the introduction of new products and technologies, including trading and distributed ledger technologies, such as cryptocurrencies, and AI technologies, has increased competition.
label: new_exposure
evidence: particularly with our own alternative trading system and our exchange-based market-making activities
reason: Competition from other alternative trading systems now explicitly names the company's own ATS, a business line last year's text did not identify as exposed; stablecoins are a sub-case of already-covered distributed ledger disruption.

title: Our products are subject to risks associated with overseas sourcing, manufacturing and financing.
label: escalated
evidence: unexpected closures, unexpected increases in work wages or other changes in labor standards and sustainability-related requirements, whether government mandated or otherwise
reason: Adds sustainability-related requirements as a cause of contractor closures and cost increases that contractors have already experienced, a concrete new driver of an existing exposure.

title: We could be subject to changes in tax rates, the adoption of new US or international tax legislation, or exposure to additional tax liabilities.
label: de_escalated
evidence: exempts US operations of US-parented companies from global minimum tax rules
reason: A new OECD safe harbor exempts US operations of US-parented companies from global minimum tax, narrowing the exposure to rules adopted outside the US.

title: Our operations could be adversely affected by events outside of our control, such as natural disasters, wars or health epidemics.
label: de_escalated
evidence: the broader consequences in the current conflict between Russia and Ukraine, which may include further embargoes, regional instability and geopolitical shifts; airspace bans relating to certain routes
reason: The specific Russia-Ukraine drivers (embargoes, airspace bans, retaliation) were dropped, while war and geopolitical risk were already covered in general terms last year.

title: The market for prime real estate is competitive.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Declines in store traffic, changes in consumer shopping behavior, shifts to digital commerce, local safety concerns or reduced profitability of certain store formats or regions could adversely affect our store strategy, lease decisions and operating results.
reason: The new sentence adds causes of loss not in last year's text, including declining store traffic, shifts to digital commerce, and local safety concerns, which could hurt store strategy and lease decisions.

title: JPMorganChase could suffer losses if the value of collateral declines.
label: new_exposure
evidence: borrowers may under-maintain or misrepresent the condition or existence of collateral, or at liquidation, collateral could be subject to competing claims
reason: Borrower collateral misrepresentation and competing claims at liquidation are new loss sources not covered last year, which addressed only value declines, liquidation shortfalls, posting failures and valuation disputes.

title: Competition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: divergent and evolving societal views and investor pressures regarding a future energy transition
reason: Reputational risk from investor views on the energy transition was already covered last year; the additions (AI, supranational objectives, societal views) are new examples or wording within existing exposures.

title: The Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions.
label: boilerplate
evidence: consumer confidence and spending can be materially adversely affected by changes in fiscal and monetary policy
reason: The changes are condensing and rewording: the headline's adverse-impact clause is dropped, but the body still describes the same economic exposures and their effects on the business.

title: The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs on the value of its inventory and other assets, in addition to purchase commitment cancellation risk.
label: boilerplate
evidence: typically for periods up to 150 days
reason: The only substantive change is dropping the 150-day commitment period detail; the company does not say the exposure shrank, so this is not a material change.

title: Acquisitions, joint ventures, investments, and divestitures could result in operating difficulties, dilution, and other consequences that could harm our business, financial condition, and operating results.
label: boilerplate
evidence: result in the payment of fees or penalties to a counterparty
reason: Adds new examples of harm from approval conditions and illiquidity, which were already covered risks. Nothing shows the risk materialising or growing, so substance is unchanged.

title: We face risks related to changes in our business strategies and plans, which have affected and may continue to affect our cost structure, the value of our assets and/or our results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: and certain hotel experiences assets
reason: The company reports a new realized write-down of hotel experiences assets, a concrete new instance of the asset-impairment harm already covered in the prior version.
